A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SLDBench and SLDAgent. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison; v5's removal of Appendix E is identifiable rather than an extraction gap.

before.justification: v3 reports original agent evaluations, human-baseline fitting, ablations and downstream application results, including Tables 2–6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v5 reports revised agent-evaluation results and retains original model-selection, hyperparameter-validation and ablation results. These qualify regardless of whether the revised entries came from reruns.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 replaces the reported discovered prediction models: SFT changes from a shifted power law to a saturated ratio form, and MoE uses a different factorization with an additional model-size term. The SLDAgent co-evolution algorithm, prompts and configuration remain unchanged; the application code in Appendix B.3 also remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight scaling-law tasks and retain the same downstream applications. The u_shape task remains represented by 389 seen and 127 unseen points across nine groups. Changing 'seven' to 'eight' corrects the summary; deleting Appendix E does not remove that benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 retain the same agent, human and model-selection comparators, and Table 6 retains the law-only ablation. Although Section 4.1 changes 'seven' to 'eight' agentic systems, no additional comparator appears in the corresponding evaluation. The Human u_shape comparison remains after Appendix E is removed.

E3.justification: The documented splits, backend models, 50-iteration budget, R² metric and clipping convention remain unchanged, as do the downstream application settings. Appendix E's deletion removes protocol detail without establishing a changed protocol for the retained u_shape task. The PDFs do not explain whether the numerical revisions involved reruns.

E4.justification: Deleting Appendix E removes the detailed investigation of extrapolation beyond an apparently monotonic training prefix, including polynomial-versus-agent curves for arithmetic, analogical similarity and Hindu knowledge. This removes a substantive analysis of non-monotonic generalization. The benchmark scores remain, while Appendix B.6's co-optimization and iteration analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run means in Tables 2–3 and the identical standard-deviation table in Appendix B.2. Table 6 still reports three-run ablation means, and Figure 4 retains its run information. There is no documented change in uncertainty-estimation practice or run counts.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 substantially revise reported values under unchanged documented settings: GPT-5 SLDAgent's average R² changes from 0.967 to 0.748, lr&bsz from 0.955 to 0.604, and u_shape from 0.928 to -0.305. All six SLDAgent backends now have negative u_shape scores, and several baseline scores and rankings also change. Section 4.3 adds a selected MoE-fit comparison of 0.891 versus 0.732; Appendix E's case results and unclipped Human score disappear. Table 4 and the hyperparameter-validation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 revises the mathematical forms and their associated reasoning. The MoE discussion now gives separate expert-count and model-size limits, explicitly conditions model-size decay on a negative fitted exponent, and qualifies the prior law's asymptotics by coefficient signs. Appendix E's model definitions disappear, while the closed-form optimizer derivation in Appendix B.4 is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion now describe eight tasks instead of seven, correcting the stated benchmark contribution to match existing coverage. The central claims about autonomous discovery, superhuman performance, principled laws and practical utility remain substantially unchanged despite the revised evidence.

C2.justification: The SFT explanation changes from unifying transferred and fine-tuning data under one exponent to dimensional consistency and interpretable parameterization; the MoE mechanism and asymptotic comparison are also revised. v5 identifies u_shape as a remaining outlier and removes Appendix E's strong non-monotonic-generalization interpretation. Section 6 adds a substantive limitation concerning overfitting and inadequate self-verification.

D1.justification: Removing Appendix E eliminates per-group u_shape thresholds and sample counts, the explicit polynomial-baseline specification, and details of the discovered law's robust fitting procedure. Other prompts, configurations and application code are retained. The first-page HuggingFace link changes from a specific dataset to a collection, changing the supplied access route.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and related-work survey remain unchanged. However, Section 4.3 revises the relationship to prior scaling laws: SFT is now described through parameterizations with comparable expressive capacity, and the criticism of the prior MoE law becomes conditional on fitted signs rather than asserting inevitable divergence.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the results discussion and law analysis. Section 6 becomes a numbered set of named limitations, appendix headings are standardized, and correspondence information is added. Appendix E is removed, but the main section sequence and most retained appendix prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with reordered bars and adjusted label and legend presentation. Appendix E's six-panel Figure 5 and Tables 7–8 are removed. The other principal figures and table structures are retained, with local reflow and updated result highlighting.

improvement.justification: v5 adds a useful overfitting limitation and corrects the task count and Human average, which now agrees with the displayed task scores. However, it removes reproducibility details for the retained u_shape task and introduces a mismatch between Section 4.3's SFT formula and the unchanged model-selection implementation in Appendix B.3.2. The major numerical and formula revisions are unexplained, leaving uncertainty about which earlier deficiencies were corrected. These benefits and losses do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
